Source format: Founding charter

2.1 The primary objective of the WGLMC shall be to establish a scientifically robust, long-term monitoring programme for leopards in the Western Ghats, using camera trap surveys, sign surveys, and wherever feasible, radio-telemetry and GPS-collaring studies.

2.2 The Cell shall compile and maintain a centralised database of leopard sightings, conflict incidents, livestock depredation cases, roadkill records, and seizure data from all participating states and union territories.

2.3 The Cell shall develop and disseminate standardised field protocols for leopard population estimation, conflict response, and mitigation measures, to be adopted by member states on a voluntary basis.

2.4 The Cell shall facilitate training programmes for forest field staff, frontline personnel, and researchers in leopard ecology, camera trap techniques, data management, and conflict resolution.

2.5 The Cell shall advise state forest departments on the identification of critical leopard habitats, corridor conservation, and the prioritisation of areas for conflict mitigation interventions.

2.6 The Cell shall promote public awareness and community engagement programmes aimed at reducing human-leopard conflict and fostering coexistence.

ARTICLE III: GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE

3.1 The operational area of the WGLMC shall cover the Western Ghats hill range and its associated eastern and western fringes, extending from the Tapti River in the north to the southern tip of the peninsula at Kanyakumari.

Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell established_date 2019-04-12 date. Record status: current.

3.2 The geographic scope shall encompass the states of Gujarat (southern districts), Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu, and the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, to the extent that these territories fall within the Western Ghats landscape.

3.3 For the purposes of monitoring and data collation, the landscape shall be divided into the following zones:

(a) Northern Western Ghats Zone: comprising the Sahyadri ranges in Maharashtra and southern Gujarat;
(b) Central Western Ghats Zone: comprising the Malenadu and coastal ranges in Goa and Karnataka;
(c) Southern Western Ghats Zone: comprising the Nilgiri, Anamalai, and Agasthyamalai ranges in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

3.4 The Steering Committee may, from time to time, revise the zonal boundaries based on ecological and administrative considerations.

ARTICLE IV: FOUNDING MEMBERS

4.1 The following persons and institutions shall be recognised as founding members of the WGLMC:

1. Dr. Meera Krishnan, Chief Wildlife Warden (Retd.), Karnataka Forest Department, Bengaluru.
2. Dr. R. S. Bopanna, Professor of Wildlife Ecology, College of Forestry, Sirsi, Karnataka.
3. Mr. Anil Kumar Salian, Deputy Conservator of Forests, Dandeli Wildlife Division, Karnataka.
4. Dr. Nandini Ramesh, Wildlife Biologist, Centre for Wildlife Studies, Bengaluru.
5. Mr. Prakash Amte, Field Director, Sahyadri Tiger Reserve, Maharashtra Forest Department.
6. Dr. K. S. Seshadri, Assistant Professor, Department of Ecology, Pondicherry University.
7. Ms. Farah Contractor, Independent Researcher, Goa.
8. Dr. B. S. Sandeep, Veterinary Officer, Kerala Forest Department, Thiruvananthapuram.
9. Mr. V. S. Ganesan, Range Forest Officer, Tirunelveli Forest Division, Tamil Nadu Forest Department.
10. Dr. Divya Karnad, Conservation Scientist, ATREE, Bengaluru.
11. Mr. Harish Bhat, Divisional Forest Officer, Belgaum Forest Division, Karnataka.
12. Dr. C. S. Prakash, Director, Institute of Wildlife Conservation and Research, Pune.

4.2 Additional members, including representatives of non-governmental organisations, independent researchers, and officers of the participating state forest departments, may be co-opted by the Steering Committee as ordinary members.
ARTICLE IV (contd.)

4.3 The Steering Committee shall maintain a register of founding members and ordinary members, noting the date of admission, institutional affiliation, and the zone in which the member primarily operates. The register shall be open to inspection by any member upon reasonable notice.

4.4 Membership shall be personal to the individual and shall not be transferable. Where a member is nominated by an institution, the institution may nominate a substitute for the remainder of the term, subject to the approval of the Steering Committee.

4.5 A member may resign by written notice to the Secretary. The Steering Committee may terminate membership by a two-thirds majority vote for conduct prejudicial to the objectives of the WGLMC, provided that the member is given an opportunity to be heard.

ARTICLE V: OFFICE-BEARERS AND THE SECRETARIAT

5.1 The WGLMC shall have the following office-bearers, elected at the first meeting of the Steering Committee:

(a) Chairperson;
(b) Vice-Chairperson;
(c) Secretary;
(d) Treasurer.

5.2 The Chairperson shall preside over meetings of the Steering Committee and the General Body, and shall represent the WGLMC in matters of policy and external relations.

5.3 The Secretary shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the WGLMC, including the maintenance of records, the issuance of notices, and the custody of the common seal.

5.4 The Treasurer shall be responsible for the receipt and disbursement of funds, and shall present an audited statement of accounts at each annual meeting.

5.5 The Secretariat shall be located at the office of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Karnataka Forest Department, Bengaluru, until such time as the Steering Committee decides otherwise.

5.6 The Secretariat shall be headed by a Coordinator, who shall be appointed by the Steering Committee. The Coordinator shall not be a member of the Steering Committee, but shall attend its meetings in an ex-officio capacity.

ARTICLE VI: THE STEERING COMMITTEE

6.1 The Steering Committee shall consist of the following:

(a) The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary, and Treasurer;
(b) The Chief Wildlife Wardens of the participating states, or their nominees;
(c) The Field Director of each tiger reserve within the landscape;
(d) The Coordinator of the WGLMC (ex-officio);
(e) Up to three co-opted members, being experts in wildlife biology, veterinary science, or social sciences, appointed for a term of two years.

6.2 The Steering Committee shall meet at least twice a year. The Secretary shall issue notice of each meeting at least fifteen days in advance, along with the agenda.

6.3 The quorum for a meeting of the Steering Committee shall be one-half of the total membership. In the absence of a quorum, the meeting shall be adjourned to a date not less than seven days later, and the members present at the adjourned meeting shall constitute the quorum.

6.4 Decisions of the Steering Committee shall be by a simple majority of members present and voting, except where a two-thirds majority is expressly required by this Charter. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.

6.5 The Steering Committee may constitute sub-committees for specific purposes, including but not limited to: the Data Standards Sub-Committee, the Field Protocols Sub-Committee, and the Training and Capacity Building Sub-Committee. Each sub-committee shall report to the Steering Committee.

ARTICLE VII: GENERAL BODY

7.1 The General Body shall consist of all founding members and ordinary members.

7.2 The General Body shall meet once a year, ordinarily during the month of April. The agenda shall include the annual report, the audited accounts, and the plan of work for the ensuing year.
CHARTER AND FOUNDING RECORDS OF THE WESTERN GHATS LEOPARD MONITORING CELL

Registered Office: C/o Wildlife Research & Conservation Division, 4th Floor, Van Bhavan, Pune, Maharashtra
Date of Charter: 12 April 2019

---

ARTICLE VIII: AMENDMENTS AND DISSOLUTION

8.1 Any amendment to this Charter may be proposed by a member of the Steering Committee or by a petition signed by not less than one-fifth of the ordinary members. Such proposal shall be circulated by the Secretary to all members at least thirty days before the meeting at which it is to be considered.

8.2 Amendments shall require a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting at a duly convened meeting of the General Body.

8.3 No amendment shall be effective unless it is consistent with the objectives set out in Article II of this Charter and with the laws of the Republic of India.

8.4 The WGLMC may be dissolved only by a resolution passed by a three-fourths majority of the General Body at a special meeting convened for that purpose. Upon dissolution, all assets and records of the Cell shall be transferred to the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, or to such other institution as the General Body may decide.

ARTICLE IX: FINANCE AND AUDIT

9.1 The financial year of the WGLMC shall be from 1 April to 31 March.

9.2 The Treasurer shall maintain proper books of account in such form as may be approved by the Steering Committee.

9.3 The accounts of the Cell shall be audited annually by a chartered accountant appointed by the General Body.

9.4 All funds of the Cell shall be kept in a bank account operated jointly by the Treasurer and the Secretary.

9.5 The Steering Committee may accept grants, donations, or other contributions from governmental agencies, philanthropic organisations, or individuals, provided that such acceptance does not compromise the independence or scientific integrity of the Cell.

ARTICLE X: RECORDS AND DATA

10.1 The Cell shall maintain a central repository of all data collected under its auspices, including but not limited to camera-trap images, scat samples, genetic analysis results, and mortality records.

10.2 The Coordinator shall be responsible for the custody of the repository and for ensuring that all data are entered in a timely manner and backed up at intervals of not more than one month.

10.3 Access to the repository shall be governed by a Data Access Policy to be framed by the Data Standards Sub-Committee and approved by the Steering Committee.

10.4 The annual report of the Cell shall include a summary of data collected and a statement of the status of the repository.

ARTICLE XI: MISCELLANEOUS

11.1 The WGLMC shall have a common seal, which shall remain in the custody of the Secretary.

11.2 The Cell may sue and be sued in its own name through the Secretary or any other officer authorised by the Steering Committee.

11.3 Any dispute arising out of the interpretation of this Charter shall be referred to the Chairperson, whose decision, after consultation with the Steering Committee, shall be final.

11.4 No member of the Cell shall derive any personal profit from the activities of the Cell, provided that reasonable expenses incurred in the discharge of official duties may be reimbursed.

Field observation log

Instructions to staff: Record all leopard sign and sightings. For direct sightings, note sex if certain, age class (A = adult, SA = subadult, C = cub), and any individual marks (e.g., collar, tail kink, ear notch). For camera trap images, record trap ID, date, time, and any identifying features. If in doubt, write "unidentified" rather than guessing. All entries to be compiled at month end by the Range Officer.

01 Nov 2023 (Wed)
0645 hrs – T. Found on dry stream bed near Kakkad Bridge, 200 m upstream of the culvert. Single pugmark, forefoot, length 8.2 cm, width 7.5 cm. Direction of travel: north-east. Likely adult male but not confirmed – no clear toe spread due to gravel. Observer: PR. (Field condition: early morning, good light, but bed was disturbed by cattle from previous day.)

0930 hrs – Sc. Collected from the same stream bed, 50 m further upstream. Two segments, 12 cm and 9 cm, containing hair and bone fragments. Sent to lab for diet analysis. Sample ID: WL-23-1101-01. Observer: PR.

1700 hrs – CT check at CT-17 (Malakkara – Kakkad trail, 1.2 km from the bridge). Camera had been placed 12 Oct 2023. Battery low (read 3.1 V), but memory card had 214 images. Downloaded and reviewed in field (see below). Camera re-baited with scent lure (commercial, same as previous). Observer: PR, AK.

CT-17 images (selected, 01 Nov):
- 14 Oct 2023, 2114 hrs – Leopard, adult, moving west. No clear view of head or body – only rump and tail. Identified as "leopard sp." only. No individual marks visible.
- 16 Oct 2023, 0530 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking toward camera. Image slightly blurred (camera shake due to wind). No collar. Sex not determinable from this image.
- 19 Oct 2023, 1935 hrs – Leopard, adult, standing broadside. Clear view of left side. No collar, no ear notch. Tail appears normal. Sex not visible (camera angle). Note: this individual may be the same as the one photographed on 16 Oct – similar size and coat pattern, but not confirmed.
- 20 Oct 2023, 0622 hrs – Leopard cub(s) – two, possibly three, moving quickly across the frame. Too fast to count precisely. No other images of cubs on the card. (See also 22 Oct entry below.)
- 24 Oct 2023, 1840 hrs – Leopard, adult, head and chest visible. No collar. Right ear has a small notch at the tip (approx. 1 cm). This mark was noted earlier in the year – see 15 Mar 2023 entry (Rani?). Sex not visible.
- 28 Oct 2023, 2230 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking away from camera. Tail held low. No marks visible.

Noted on card: CT-17 is on a well-used game trail. Frequency of leopard images appears higher than last month (Sep: 11 images; Oct: 17 images). Possibly a female with cubs using this area. Will monitor.

---

12 Dec 2023 (Tue)
Field day. 0715 hrs – T. on the jeep track again, same location as 08 Dec. Two pugmarks, adult, forefeet. Lengths 7.5 and 7.8 cm. Direction: west. Same individual, likely. PK noted the track was slightly deeper than the previous set, suggesting the animal was moving faster or carrying weight.

0930 hrs – Direct sighting. PK and I were on the west fireline, near the bamboo thicket where AK saw the leopard on 08 Dec. 0930 hrs – Leopard, adult, came out of the thicket and walked along the fireline for about 40 m, then stopped and sat down facing east. We watched it for about 2 minutes at a distance of ~80 m. The right ear notch was visible. No collar. The leopard then stood up, walked into the thicket, and disappeared. PK noted the same large body size as AK described. We both tried to see the genital area when it sat down, but the angle was still side-on and the vegetation partially blocked the view. PK said he could not confirm sex. I noted "possible male, not confirmed" in my field book.

We also checked CT-19 and CT-20 on the east side. No leopard images. CT-19 had a civet and a mongoose. CT-20 had a group of langurs.

Leopard Individual 'Shiva' sex female. Record status: current.

---

13 Dec 2023 (Wed)
No field work – light rain all day. HQ. I began compiling the December camera trap summary. So far in December we have had 6 leopard detections on the west side (CT-17, CT-18) and 2 on the east side (CT-19, CT-20, but those were on 01 and 03 Dec and may be a different individual – smaller body size, no ear notch visible). I have not yet compared the east and west individuals side by side.

I also received the preliminary report from the genetics lab on an older scat sample (SC-098, collected 22 Nov). The report says the sample was too degraded for a reliable sex determination. They recommend a fresh sample. I have noted this in the log and will keep SC-114 in mind.

---

14 Dec 2023 (Thu)
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-4. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – I checked CT-21 and CT-22 on the south boundary. CT-21 had 1 image of a leopard at 0145 hrs on 13 Dec – walking toward the camera, head and chest visible, right ear notch clearly visible. Same individual. No sex visible – the image cuts off at the shoulder. CT-22 had no leopard images, but had a good sequence of a porcupine.

1100 hrs – AK called on the radio. He was on the east side and had found fresh pugmarks near the stream crossing at E-2. He described them as adult, forefeet, lengths 7.3 and 7.6 cm, direction north. He said the size was slightly smaller than the west fireline tracks we have been measuring. He thought it might be a different individual, possibly a female. I noted this in the log but did not mark it as confirmed – we need more data before assigning a new individual.

---

15 Dec 2023 (Fri)
HQ day. I spent the morning on the ID sheet. I added a row for the possible east side individual – "unidentified, smaller adult, possible female, seen on CT-19/CT-20 and tracks at E-2." Status: provisional. I also added a note that the west fireline leopard remains "unknown sex, possible male" pending scat results or a clear image.
Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell

---

**16 Dec 2023 (Sat)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK and I walked the lower ridge transect R-1 to R-4 again, this time looking specifically for scat after the rain. Found one old scat (SC-116) near R-2, likely 5-7 days old, sun-bleached, no visible prey remains. Collected anyway for the genetics backlog; labeled clearly as degraded. 0945 hrs – AK radioed from the east side. He had re-checked the stream crossing at E-2 and found the same set of pugmarks from 14 Dec now partially washed out by the rain. He took fresh photos for the record, but they are not good enough for measurement. He also reported a possible scrape on a fallen log about 40 m north of the crossing – fresh, maybe 1-2 days old. I told him to mark it with flagging and we will check it together on Monday.

No camera trap images to review today – the batteries on CT-19 are low and we did not have spares with us. Will replace on Monday.

---

**17 Dec 2023 (Sun)**
HQ. Sunday – no field work. I went through the camera trap images from CT-21 and CT-22 for the past week. CT-21 had one more leopard image, this time on 15 Dec at 2210 hrs – same right ear notch, walking away from the camera, full body visible. Still no sex determination possible – the image is backlit and the tail obscures the underside. CT-22 had no leopard images. I also reviewed the CT-19 and CT-20 images from 01 and 03 Dec again, side by side with the CT-21 individual. The east side individual is smaller in the shoulder-to-rump length, and the ear notch is not visible in any of the east images. I am fairly confident they are two different animals, but I have not formally separated them on the ID sheet yet – will do that when we have a clearer east side image.

---

**18 Dec 2023 (Mon)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK, AK, and I went to the east side to check the scrape at E-2 and replace the CT-19 batteries. The scrape was still there but had been rained on – no fresh scent detectable. We set up a temporary camera trap (CT-23) on the log, facing the scrape, to see if the individual returns. 1100 hrs – we walked the east fireline from E-1 to E-5. No fresh sign until E-4, where we found a small pile of scat (SC-117) – very fresh, still moist, with hair and small bone fragments visible. Collected for genetics. This is the first fresh scat we have found on the east side in December. I am hopeful this will give us a sex determination for the east side individual.

---

**19 Dec 2023 (Tue)**
HQ day. I updated the ID sheet with the December camera trap summary. West side (CT-17, CT-18): 6 detections, all of the same ear-notched individual. East side (CT-19, CT-20): 2 detections, smaller individual, no ear notch. Provisional status for the east side individual remains. I also noted that CT-23 is now active on the east side.

In the afternoon, I called the genetics lab about SC-117. They said they will prioritize it if we mark it as high priority – I did, since we need the sex determination for the east side individual. They said we should have results in 2-3 weeks.

---

**20 Dec 2023 (Wed)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-4. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – I checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had 2 leopard images from 18 Dec – one at 0230 hrs (walking toward camera, head and chest visible, right ear notch clearly visible) and one at 0410 hrs (same individual, walking away). No sex visible in either. CT-22 had no leopard images. 1100 hrs – I checked CT-23 on the east side. No leopard images yet, but the camera is working well – good test images of a sambar deer.

---

---

**22 Dec 2023 (Fri)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – I checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had 1 leopard image from 20 Dec at 1945 hrs – same ear-notched individual, walking along the trail. CT-22 had no leopard images. 1100 hrs – I checked CT-23 and CT-24 on the east side. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had 2 leopard images from 21 Dec – one at 0145 hrs and one at 0310 hrs, both of the same individual. The images are not clear enough to determine sex, but the individual appears to be the same smaller size as the east side individual from CT-19/CT-20. I noted this in the log.
**Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell**

---

**23 Dec 2023 (Sat)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-4. No fresh sign. 0945 hrs – checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had no leopard images. CT-22 had 1 leopard image from 22 Dec at 2130 hrs – poor light, only the hindquarters visible. Could not confirm identity. 1100 hrs – checked CT-23 and CT-24 on the east side. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had no new leopard images beyond the 21 Dec set.

Afternoon – walked the east side stream bed from the CT-24 junction down to the old boulder pile. Found a scrape on a fallen log approx. 40 m below the junction. Fresh, likely from last night. No scat nearby. Took GPS point (E-112) and photos. Scrape is consistent with a small individual – claw marks on the log are narrow, spacing tight. Noted for the ID sheet.

---

**24 Dec 2023 (Sun)**
HQ day. Compiled the week's camera trap summary for the ID sheet.

West side (CT-17, CT-18): 9 detections this week, all ear-notched individual. Times range 0130–0500 hrs and one at 2215 hrs on 23 Dec. No sex visible in any image.

East side (CT-19, CT-20, CT-24): 4 detections total. CT-19 – 1 image on 20 Dec (smaller individual, no ear notch, head only). CT-20 – 0. CT-24 – 2 images on 21 Dec (same smaller individual, both walking away from camera). No sex determination possible from any of these. Provisional status for the east side individual remains unchanged – male or female unknown.

Also reviewed the scrape photos from yesterday. The scrape dimensions (approx. 18 cm long, 8 cm wide) and the narrow claw spacing suggest a smaller animal, but this is not diagnostic. Noted in the log.

Called the genetics lab about SC-117 again. They confirmed it is in the extraction queue, expected results in 2-3 weeks. The lab asked if we could send a second scat sample if we find one – they said a second sample would help them confirm the sex determination if the first one comes back weak. I said we would try.

---

**26 Dec 2023 (Tue)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had 1 leopard image from 24 Dec at 0245 hrs – ear-notched individual, walking toward camera, chest and front legs visible. No sex visible. CT-22 had no leopard images. 1100 hrs – checked CT-23 and CT-24. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had 1 leopard image from 25 Dec at 1915 hrs – same smaller individual, walking along the trail, but the image is dark and the animal is partly obscured by vegetation. No sex visible.

I also checked the trap at CT-25 – this is the new location we moved from CT-16 last week. No leopard images yet. The camera is positioned on a game trail that connects the east side stream bed to the upper ridge. I am hopeful this will give us more east side detections.

---

**27 Dec 2023 (Wed)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the upper ridge transect, R-5 to R-7. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – checked CT-25. Still no leopard images. The camera had test images of a barking deer and a wild pig. 1100 hrs – walked the east side stream bed again, from the boulder pile down to the old log crossing. Found pugmarks in the mud near the crossing – approx. 6.5 cm long, 5.5 cm wide. Smaller than the west side individual's pugmarks. Took photos and measurements. The pugmarks are consistent with the smaller east side individual, but I could not determine sex from the tracks.

In the afternoon, I reviewed the camera trap images from the past week with PK. We compared the east side individual's images from CT-19, CT-20, and CT-24. The size difference from the west side individual is consistent across all images – the east side animal is noticeably smaller, with a slimmer build. We also noted that the east side individual seems to be more active in the late evening (1900–2000 hrs) and early morning (0100–0300 hrs), while the west side individual is active through the night. This is preliminary – we only have a handful of detections.
**Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell**

---

**28 Dec 2023 (Thu)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-3. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – checked CT-21, CT-22, CT-23. All had no leopard images. CT-22 had a sequence of wild pig moving through at 0345 hrs, and CT-23 had a sambar hind with calf at dusk. 1100 hrs – checked CT-25. Two leopard images from last night: 0130 hrs and 0215 hrs. Both show the smaller east side individual, moving east to west along the game trail. The 0130 image is clear – head and shoulder visible, no ear notch on the left ear, right ear not visible. Still no sex visible. The 0215 image is from behind, tail and hindquarters only.

Noted that CT-25 is picking up more activity than the old CT-16 location did in the same period. The game trail connects the east side stream bed to the upper ridge, and we are getting regular use. PK suggested we might move CT-19 to the southern end of the east side stream bed to cover the other approach, but I want more data from CT-25 first. We will revisit in the new year.

---

**29 Dec 2023 (Fri)**
No field day. Office work – data entry and image review. Catalogued the December images from all cameras. December totals by camera (leopard detections only):

| Camera | Detections | Individual | Notes |
|--------|------------|------------|-------|
| CT-19  | 4          | East side  | All after 2100 hrs |
| CT-20  | 3          | East side  | One image 19 Dec – good left flank view |
| CT-21  | 2          | West side  | 24 Dec – ear-notched, chest/front legs |
| CT-22  | 0          | –          | – |
| CT-23  | 1          | East side  | 25 Dec – dark, partly obscured |
| CT-24  | 1          | East side  | 25 Dec – dark, partly obscured |
| CT-25  | 2          | East side  | 28 Dec – clear head/shoulder, no ear notch |

Total: 13 leopard detections in December. This is higher than November (9 detections). The increase is mostly from the east side individual, which was detected 4 times in November and 8 times in December. The west side individual was detected 5 times in November and 2 times in December. This shift might reflect seasonal movement or could be a result of the camera relocation. We will not draw conclusions until we have another full month of data.

---

**31 Dec 2023 (Sun)**
Short field day. 0800 hrs – PK checked CT-25 and CT-24. CT-25 had no new leopard images. CT-24 had 1 leopard image from 30 Dec at 2245 hrs – the smaller east side individual, walking along the trail. The image is better than the 25 Dec image – the animal is in full view, side profile. I could see the tail clearly – it appears to have a slight kink near the tip. Not sure if this is a distinguishing feature or just the angle. No sex visible.

I also checked the pugmark site near the old log crossing. The mud has dried, so no fresh tracks. The earlier pugmark measurements (6.5 cm long, 5.5 cm wide) are on file.

---

**02 Jan 2024 (Tue)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the upper ridge transect. No fresh sign. 0900 hrs – checked CT-23, CT-24, CT-25. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had 1 leopard image from 01 Jan at 1915 hrs – the smaller east side individual, walking toward the camera. The image is clear – head, chest, and front legs visible. Still no sex visible. CT-25 had 1 leopard image from 01 Jan at 0230 hrs – same individual, walking east to west. The image is from the side – full body visible. The animal appears to be in good condition, no visible injuries or marks on the body.

Noted that the east side individual is consistently using the CT-25 trail at night, mostly between 0130 and 0230 hrs. The 1915 hrs detection at CT-24 is earlier than usual – most east side detections are after 2100 hrs. This could be a one-off or could indicate a shift in activity pattern. We will keep tracking.
**03 Jan 2024 (Wed)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK and RS on the lower stream transect. Fresh scat found at the stream crossing, approx. 30 m upstream of the old log crossing. Scat was dark, segmented, with hair and bone fragments; too old to collect for diet analysis (estimated 2–3 days). Photographed in place and left. GPS: N 15°22.841', E 74°18.552'. No other sign on the transect.

0930 hrs – checked CT-26, which we had not visited since the 28 Dec relocation. CT-26 had 2 leopard images, both from 01 Jan, both the west side individual. First image at 2145 hrs, walking west to east. Second image at 2252 hrs, same direction. In the second image the animal pauses and appears to scent-mark – the tail is raised and there is a visible spray. The image is slightly overexposed but the behavior is clear. This is the first time we have captured marking behavior at CT-26 since the relocation. Will note this in the monthly behavior summary.

---

**05 Jan 2024 (Fri)**
Short field day. 0830 hrs – PK checked CT-24 only. No new leopard images. CT-24 battery at 62%, SD card 45% full. Replaced SD card and battery as per the 3-month rotation schedule. Old card filed with the Dec data.

Heard vocalization from the east ridge at approx. 0930 hrs – a series of hoarse coughs, repeated 3 times, lasting about 10 seconds total. Could not locate the animal visually. Direction was consistent with the east side individual's known range. Noted in the vocalization log. No other observations.

---

**07 Jan 2024 (Sun)**
Field day. 0645 hrs – PK and RS on the upper ridge transect, continuing the sign survey from 02 Jan. No fresh pugmarks, but found 2 scrape marks on the ridge crest, approx. 200 m apart. Both scrapes were shallow, with a small pile of loose soil and leaf litter at the rear. The first scrape had a few strands of hair caught on a low branch above it – likely from the animal rubbing or marking. Hair sample collected and stored in the dry box (sample ID H-012). The second scrape had no hair, but the soil was still damp underneath, suggesting it was made within the last 24–36 hrs.

1100 hrs – checked CT-23. No leopard images since the 01 Jan image. CT-23 has been quiet for 6 days now. Considering moving the camera to the scrape site on the ridge crest, but will wait until the end of the month to avoid confounding the monthly detection comparison. The scrape site is not on a well-defined trail, so a camera may not capture much. Will discuss with the team.

---

**09 Jan 2024 (Tue)**
Field day. 0730 hrs – PK on the lower stream transect. Found fresh pugmarks along the stream bank, approx. 50 m downstream of the old log crossing. The mud was soft and the tracks were clear. Measured the largest track: 7.0 cm long, 6.0 cm wide – this is larger than the December pugmark (6.5 cm × 5.5 cm) and is consistent with the west side individual's size. The track set continued along the bank for about 15 m, then turned upslope toward the west ridge. No other sign in the area.

Also heard a leopard calling from the west ridge at approx. 0915 hrs – a series of sawing calls, repeated for about 20 seconds. This is the first time we have heard this call type in the west side's range. The animal was not seen. The vocalization log now has 4 entries for the month: 2 from the east side, 2 from the west side.

---

**11 Jan 2024 (Thu)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK and RS checked CT-25 and CT-24. CT-25 had 1 leopard image from 10 Jan at 0205 hrs – the east side individual, walking west to east. Image is clear, full body side profile. The tail kink near the tip is visible again – consistent with the 30 Dec image. No sex visible. CT-24 had no leopard images.

Noted that the east side individual's activity is still mostly between 0130 and 0230 hrs at CT-25. The 02 Jan detection at 1915 hrs at CT-24 remains the only exception. Will keep tracking to see if this pattern holds.
**Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell**
**(WGLMC – Field Log S02)**

**Month: January 2024 (continued)**
**Location: WGLMC Study Area, Western Ghats**
**Observer(s): PK, RS, VN, AS**

---

**13 Jan 2024 (Sat)**
Field day. 0645 hrs – PK and VN conducted a scat survey along the mid-elevation ridge line (Transect R-2). Located 3 scats. Scat 1 was on the main trail, approx. 30 m east of the large banyan. Scat 2 was near the base of a rocky outcrop, partly covered with leaf litter. Scat 3 was on a small game trail leading downslope toward the stream. All scats were collected. Scat 1 and Scat 3 were placed in paper bags and will be processed for DNA analysis. Scat 2 was too old and dry (approx. 2–3 weeks old) – discarded.

Also checked CT-26 and CT-27. CT-26 had no leopard images. CT-27 had 1 image of a sambar deer, no leopard. The camera at CT-27 was slightly misaligned – the branch in front of the lens had grown and was partially blocking the field of view. Will clear the branch next visit.

---

**15 Jan 2024 (Mon)**
Field day. 0730 hrs – RS and AS checked CT-28 and CT-29. CT-28 had no leopard images. CT-29 had 2 leopard images from 14 Jan at 2215 hrs and 2230 hrs. Both images show the same individual – appears to be the west side individual, but head is partially obscured in both frames. The tail kink is not visible. Body size is consistent with the west side individual. No sex visible.

Noted that the west side individual's activity at CT-29 is at a new time – 2215–2230 hrs. Previous detections of this individual were mostly between 0030 and 0200 hrs. This is the first late-evening detection for this individual. Will monitor to see if this is a pattern change or a one-off.

---

**17 Jan 2024 (Wed)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK and VN checked CT-30 and CT-31. CT-30 had no leopard images. CT-31 had 1 leopard image from 16 Jan at 2345 hrs – the east side individual, walking north to south. The tail kink is visible. No sex visible.

Also found fresh pugmarks on the upper stream transect, approx. 100 m upstream of the waterfall. The tracks were in soft mud and were clear. Measured the largest track: 6.8 cm long, 5.7 cm wide. This is smaller than the 09 Jan track (7.0 cm × 6.0 cm) but larger than the December track (6.5 cm × 5.5 cm). This could be a different individual or the same individual with slight variation. No other sign in the area.

---

**19 Jan 2024 (Fri)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK and RS conducted a direct sighting survey along the western ridge. No leopard seen. However, at approx. 0845 hrs, heard a leopard calling from the north slope – a series of sawing calls, repeated for about 15 seconds. This is the first time we have heard the call from the north slope. The vocalization log now has 5 entries for the month: 2 from the east side, 2 from the west side, 1 from the north slope.

The north slope vocalization is new. We have not previously recorded calls from that area. The call was too distant to determine the direction of travel. Will note this in the monthly summary.

---

**21 Jan 2024 (Sun)**
Field day. 0645 hrs – VN and AS checked CT-32 and CT-33. CT-32 had no leopard images. CT-33 had 1 leopard image from 20 Jan at 0130 hrs – the east side individual, walking east to west. The tail kink is visible. No sex visible.

CT-33 is a new location for the east side individual. Previous detections of this individual were at CT-25 and CT-24. This is the first detection at CT-33. The camera is located on a narrow game trail that connects the eastern and western slopes. This suggests the east side individual is using a wider range than previously thought.

---

**23 Jan 2024 (Tue)**
Field day. 0730 hrs – PK and VN checked CT-34 and CT-35. CT-34 had no leopard images. CT-35 had 2 leopard images from 22 Jan at 0205 hrs and 0215 hrs – the west side individual. Both images are clear, full body side profile. The tail kink is not visible in either image, but the body size is consistent with the west side individual. No sex visible.

documents.title: Charter and Founding Records of the Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell
documents.content:
2.1 The primary objective of the WGLMC shall be to establish a scientifically robust, long-term monitoring programme for leopards in the Western Ghats, using camera trap surveys, sign surveys, and wherever feasible, radio-telemetry and GPS-collaring studies.

2.2 The Cell shall compile and maintain a centralised database of leopard sightings, conflict incidents, livestock depredation cases, roadkill records, and seizure data from all participating states and union territories.

2.3 The Cell shall develop and disseminate standardised field protocols for leopard population estimation, conflict response, and mitigation measures, to be adopted by member states on a voluntary basis.

2.4 The Cell shall facilitate training programmes for forest field staff, frontline personnel, and researchers in leopard ecology, camera trap techniques, data management, and conflict resolution.

2.5 The Cell shall advise state forest departments on the identification of critical leopard habitats, corridor conservation, and the prioritisation of areas for conflict mitigation interventions.

2.6 The Cell shall promote public awareness and community engagement programmes aimed at reducing human-leopard conflict and fostering coexistence.

ARTICLE III: GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE

3.1 The operational area of the WGLMC shall cover the Western Ghats hill range and its associated eastern and western fringes, extending from the Tapti River in the north to the southern tip of the peninsula at Kanyakumari.

Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell established_date 2019-04-12 date. Record status: current.

3.2 The geographic scope shall encompass the states of Gujarat (southern districts), Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu, and the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, to the extent that these territories fall within the Western Ghats landscape.

3.3 For the purposes of monitoring and data collation, the landscape shall be divided into the following zones:

(a) Northern Western Ghats Zone: comprising the Sahyadri ranges in Maharashtra and southern Gujarat;
(b) Central Western Ghats Zone: comprising the Malenadu and coastal ranges in Goa and Karnataka;
(c) Southern Western Ghats Zone: comprising the Nilgiri, Anamalai, and Agasthyamalai ranges in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

3.4 The Steering Committee may, from time to time, revise the zonal boundaries based on ecological and administrative considerations.

ARTICLE IV: FOUNDING MEMBERS

4.1 The following persons and institutions shall be recognised as founding members of the WGLMC:

1. Dr. Meera Krishnan, Chief Wildlife Warden (Retd.), Karnataka Forest Department, Bengaluru.
2. Dr. R. S. Bopanna, Professor of Wildlife Ecology, College of Forestry, Sirsi, Karnataka.
3. Mr. Anil Kumar Salian, Deputy Conservator of Forests, Dandeli Wildlife Division, Karnataka.
4. Dr. Nandini Ramesh, Wildlife Biologist, Centre for Wildlife Studies, Bengaluru.
5. Mr. Prakash Amte, Field Director, Sahyadri Tiger Reserve, Maharashtra Forest Department.
6. Dr. K. S. Seshadri, Assistant Professor, Department of Ecology, Pondicherry University.
7. Ms. Farah Contractor, Independent Researcher, Goa.
8. Dr. B. S. Sandeep, Veterinary Officer, Kerala Forest Department, Thiruvananthapuram.
9. Mr. V. S. Ganesan, Range Forest Officer, Tirunelveli Forest Division, Tamil Nadu Forest Department.
10. Dr. Divya Karnad, Conservation Scientist, ATREE, Bengaluru.
11. Mr. Harish Bhat, Divisional Forest Officer, Belgaum Forest Division, Karnataka.
12. Dr. C. S. Prakash, Director, Institute of Wildlife Conservation and Research, Pune.

4.2 Additional members, including representatives of non-governmental organisations, independent researchers, and officers of the participating state forest departments, may be co-opted by the Steering Committee as ordinary members.

ARTICLE IV (contd.)

4.3 The Steering Committee shall maintain a register of founding members and ordinary members, noting the date of admission, institutional affiliation, and the zone in which the member primarily operates. The register shall be open to inspection by any member upon reasonable notice.

4.4 Membership shall be personal to the individual and shall not be transferable. Where a member is nominated by an institution, the institution may nominate a substitute for the remainder of the term, subject to the approval of the Steering Committee.

4.5 A member may resign by written notice to the Secretary. The Steering Committee may terminate membership by a two-thirds majority vote for conduct prejudicial to the objectives of the WGLMC, provided that the member is given an opportunity to be heard.

ARTICLE V: OFFICE-BEARERS AND THE SECRETARIAT

5.1 The WGLMC shall have the following office-bearers, elected at the first meeting of the Steering Committee:

(a) Chairperson;
(b) Vice-Chairperson;
(c) Secretary;
(d) Treasurer.

5.2 The Chairperson shall preside over meetings of the Steering Committee and the General Body, and shall represent the WGLMC in matters of policy and external relations.

5.3 The Secretary shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the WGLMC, including the maintenance of records, the issuance of notices, and the custody of the common seal.

5.4 The Treasurer shall be responsible for the receipt and disbursement of funds, and shall present an audited statement of accounts at each annual meeting.

5.5 The Secretariat shall be located at the office of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Karnataka Forest Department, Bengaluru, until such time as the Steering Committee decides otherwise.

5.6 The Secretariat shall be headed by a Coordinator, who shall be appointed by the Steering Committee. The Coordinator shall not be a member of the Steering Committee, but shall attend its meetings in an ex-officio capacity.

ARTICLE VI: THE STEERING COMMITTEE

6.1 The Steering Committee shall consist of the following:

(a) The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary, and Treasurer;
(b) The Chief Wildlife Wardens of the participating states, or their nominees;
(c) The Field Director of each tiger reserve within the landscape;
(d) The Coordinator of the WGLMC (ex-officio);
(e) Up to three co-opted members, being experts in wildlife biology, veterinary science, or social sciences, appointed for a term of two years.

6.2 The Steering Committee shall meet at least twice a year. The Secretary shall issue notice of each meeting at least fifteen days in advance, along with the agenda.

6.3 The quorum for a meeting of the Steering Committee shall be one-half of the total membership. In the absence of a quorum, the meeting shall be adjourned to a date not less than seven days later, and the members present at the adjourned meeting shall constitute the quorum.

6.4 Decisions of the Steering Committee shall be by a simple majority of members present and voting, except where a two-thirds majority is expressly required by this Charter. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.

6.5 The Steering Committee may constitute sub-committees for specific purposes, including but not limited to: the Data Standards Sub-Committee, the Field Protocols Sub-Committee, and the Training and Capacity Building Sub-Committee. Each sub-committee shall report to the Steering Committee.

ARTICLE VII: GENERAL BODY

7.1 The General Body shall consist of all founding members and ordinary members.

7.2 The General Body shall meet once a year, ordinarily during the month of April. The agenda shall include the annual report, the audited accounts, and the plan of work for the ensuing year.

ARTICLE VIII: AMENDMENTS AND DISSOLUTION

8.1 Any amendment to this Charter may be proposed by a member of the Steering Committee or by a petition signed by not less than one-fifth of the ordinary members. Such proposal shall be circulated by the Secretary to all members at least thirty days before the meeting at which it is to be considered.

8.2 Amendments shall require a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting at a duly convened meeting of the General Body.

8.3 No amendment shall be effective unless it is consistent with the objectives set out in Article II of this Charter and with the laws of the Republic of India.

8.4 The WGLMC may be dissolved only by a resolution passed by a three-fourths majority of the General Body at a special meeting convened for that purpose. Upon dissolution, all assets and records of the Cell shall be transferred to the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, or to such other institution as the General Body may decide.

ARTICLE IX: FINANCE AND AUDIT

9.1 The financial year of the WGLMC shall be from 1 April to 31 March.

9.5 The Steering Committee may accept grants, donations, or other contributions from governmental agencies, philanthropic organisations, or individuals, provided that such acceptance does not compromise the independence or scientific integrity of the Cell.

ARTICLE X: RECORDS AND DATA

10.1 The Cell shall maintain a central repository of all data collected under its auspices, including but not limited to camera-trap images, scat samples, genetic analysis results, and mortality records.

10.2 The Coordinator shall be responsible for the custody of the repository and for ensuring that all data are entered in a timely manner and backed up at intervals of not more than one month.

documents.title: Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell
documents.content:
Instructions to staff: Record all leopard sign and sightings. For direct sightings, note sex if certain, age class (A = adult, SA = subadult, C = cub), and any individual marks (e.g., collar, tail kink, ear notch). For camera trap images, record trap ID, date, time, and any identifying features. If in doubt, write "unidentified" rather than guessing. All entries to be compiled at month end by the Range Officer.

---

01 Nov 2023 (Wed)
0645 hrs – T. Found on dry stream bed near Kakkad Bridge, 200 m upstream of the culvert. Single pugmark, forefoot, length 8.2 cm, width 7.5 cm. Direction of travel: north-east. Likely adult male but not confirmed – no clear toe spread due to gravel. Observer: PR. (Field condition: early morning, good light, but bed was disturbed by cattle from previous day.)

0930 hrs – Sc. Collected from the same stream bed, 50 m further upstream. Two segments, 12 cm and 9 cm, containing hair and bone fragments. Sent to lab for diet analysis. Sample ID: WL-23-1101-01. Observer: PR.

1700 hrs – CT check at CT-17 (Malakkara – Kakkad trail, 1.2 km from the bridge). Camera had been placed 12 Oct 2023. Battery low (read 3.1 V), but memory card had 214 images. Downloaded and reviewed in field (see below). Camera re-baited with scent lure (commercial, same as previous). Observer: PR, AK.

CT-17 images (selected, 01 Nov):
- 14 Oct 2023, 2114 hrs – Leopard, adult, moving west. No clear view of head or body – only rump and tail. Identified as "leopard sp." only. No individual marks visible.
- 16 Oct 2023, 0530 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking toward camera. Image slightly blurred (camera shake due to wind). No collar. Sex not determinable from this image.
- 19 Oct 2023, 1935 hrs – Leopard, adult, standing broadside. Clear view of left side. No collar, no ear notch. Tail appears normal. Sex not visible (camera angle). Note: this individual may be the same as the one photographed on 16 Oct – similar size and coat pattern, but not confirmed.
- 20 Oct 2023, 0622 hrs – Leopard cub(s) – two, possibly three, moving quickly across the frame. Too fast to count precisely. No other images of cubs on the card. (See also 22 Oct entry below.)
- 24 Oct 2023, 1840 hrs – Leopard, adult, head and chest visible. No collar. Right ear has a small notch at the tip (approx. 1 cm). This mark was noted earlier in the year – see 15 Mar 2023 entry (Rani?). Sex not visible.
- 28 Oct 2023, 2230 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking away from camera. Tail held low. No marks visible.

Noted on card: CT-17 is on a well-used game trail. Frequency of leopard images appears higher than last month (Sep: 11 images; Oct: 17 images). Possibly a female with cubs using this area. Will monitor.

---

02 Nov 2023 (Thu)
No field work – heavy rain. HQ only.

Leopard Individual 'Rani' sex female. Record status: current.

---

03 Nov 2023 (Fri)
0715 hrs – T. Found on the jeep track leading to the old teak plantation, 300 m from the main road. Two pugmarks, both forefeet, adult. Length 7.9 cm and 8.1 cm. Width 6.8 cm and 7.0 cm. Direction: south. These are smaller than the 01 Nov track – possibly a female. Marked as "unidentified, likely female" in the field, but not confirmed. Observer: AK.

1030 hrs – CT check at CT-18 (old teak plantation, 1.5 km from the road). Camera placed 10 Oct 2023. Card had 89 images. No leopard images this period. One wild dog (dhole) image, 30 Oct, 0645 hrs. One sambar hind with calf, 31 Oct, 1700 hrs. Camera functioning normally, but the trail appears less used than CT-17. Observer: AK.

---

04 Nov 2023 (Sat)
1700 hrs – S. Direct sighting, unconfirmed sex. Observed from the watchtower at Malakkara tank, 500 m east of the tank bund. A single leopard, adult, walked along the eastern bank for approx. 2 minutes, then entered the tall grass. Light was fading, but the individual appeared to be of medium size. No marks visible (distance approx. 150 m). Observer: PR, with VK (forest watcher). No photograph taken (camera in bag, not ready).

No field work – weekly rest day. (Range HQ closed for field operations.)

Leopard Individual 'Kali' sex male. Record status: current.

- 21 Nov, 1915 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking toward camera. Head and chest visible. Right ear notch visible. Same individual.
- 22 Nov, 0410 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking away. Tail held low. No marks.
- 23 Nov, 2230 hrs – Leopard, adult, sitting at edge of frame. Only left side visible. No ear notch visible.

No other leopards. The individual is using this trail regularly, roughly every 2-3 days. Still no sex confirmation. Will review the 24 Nov full body images more carefully on the laptop – sometimes the genital area is visible in the hindquarters but not obvious on the camera screen.

I can see what looks like a scrotum, but the image is slightly blurry. Not confident enough to record sex. Will flag this image for AK to review – he has more experience with this. If he agrees, we can update the ID sheet.

documents.content:
1030 hrs – Scat on the jeep track, 1.5 km from main road. Fresh, dark, segmented, ~14 cm length. Contains hair and bone fragments. Collected for diet analysis. Sample ID: SC-143. Location: 15.1234 N, 74.5678 E (approx). Observer: AK.

04 Dec 2023 (Mon)
No field work – HQ day. Updated the individual ID sheet for CT-17 trail leopard. Current status:
- Ear notch: right ear, clearly visible in 25 Nov 0330 hrs image.
- Sex: unknown, possible male (pending clearer image).
- Collar: none observed.
- Frequency: using CT-17 trail every 2-3 days; also using CT-18 bund crossing.
- Range: area between CT-17 and CT-18, approx. 1.2 km.

AK suggested we consider a camera placement at the ridge saddle between CT-17 and CT-18, where the trail narrows. If the leopard passes through the saddle, we might get a better side-on view for sex confirmation. Will discuss with the range officer about permission – the saddle is just inside the core area.

---

05 Dec 2023 (Tue)
No field work – vehicle breakdown. Waiting for spare parts from the divisional office.

---

06 Dec 2023 (Wed)
No field work – vehicle still not repaired. Did desk work: compiled the last month of CT-17 and CT-18 data into the monthly summary. Leopard detections: CT-17 – 9 images across 4 passes; CT-18 – 2 images across 2 passes. All consistent with a single individual based on ear notch and body size. No other leopard detections in the two cameras.

---

Leopard Individual 'Bheema' sex male. Record status: current.

07 Dec 2023 (Thu)
Field day – borrowed vehicle from the neighbouring range. 0700 hrs – CT check at CT-17. Card had 51 images since 02 Dec. Leopard images: 3.
- 04 Dec, 2210 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking right to left. Full body visible. No collar. No genital area visible – body angled away from camera.
- 05 Dec, 0230 hrs – Leopard, adult, sitting at edge of frame, facing away. Only back and tail visible.
- 06 Dec, 1830 hrs – Leopard, adult, walking toward camera. Head and chest visible. Right ear notch visible. Same individual.

Still no sex confirmation. The 04 Dec full body image is angled such that the hindquarters are turned away. Noted that the leopard seems to be moving through the area more often now – 3 passes in 4 days vs the earlier 2-3 day interval. Possibly due to prey movement or the recent rain.

---

08 Dec 2023 (Fri)
Field day. 0730 hrs – T. on the jeep track, 600 m from main road. Two pugmarks, both forefeet, adult. Lengths 7.6 and 7.9 cm. Widths 6.5 and 6.8 cm. Direction: west. Observer: PK. Marked as "unidentified, likely same individual" in the field.

1100 hrs – Direct sighting. AK and PK were on the fireline near the west boundary, ~300 m from the ridge. 1100 hrs – Leopard, adult, crossed the fireline from east to west at a distance of ~60 m. Walked slowly, paused to look back once, then continued into the bamboo thicket. Observed for approx. 30 seconds. AK noted the right ear notch – same individual as CT-17. No collar. Body size large, shoulder height noticeably higher than the usual females we have on camera. AK said he could not clearly see the genital area as the leopard was side-on and moving, but he noted the overall build was consistent with a male. He said he would note it as "probable male based on body size, pending visual confirmation" in his field notes.

---

09 Dec 2023 (Sat)
No field work – HQ day. AK and I discussed the leopard. AK is fairly confident it is a male based on the body size and the direct sighting, but he agrees we should wait for a clear image or a confirmed scat sample before updating the ID sheet. We decided to keep the status as "unknown sex, possible male" for now. We also discussed the possibility of collaring this individual if we can confirm it is a male and if the range officer approves – a male collar would give us good data on ranging behaviour and dispersal. But that is a decision for the higher authorities.

---

documents.title: Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell
documents.content:
CT-18 had 3 images of a sambar deer and 2 of a wild pig. No leopard.

---

11 Dec 2023 (Mon)
HQ day. I updated the individual ID sheet for the "west fireline leopard" with the new CT-17 images. Current status remains "unknown sex, possible male" based on AK's direct sighting and the large body size. I noted in the remarks column that the scat sample SC-114 is pending lab results and may help with sex ID.

AK came by the office in the afternoon. He looked at the CT-17 images again and said the shoulder height still looks male to him, but he admitted it is not conclusive. He suggested we try to get a full body image with the hindquarters visible. He also said the leopard's right ear notch is the best field marker we have – easier to pick out than the tail pattern.

---

12 Dec 2023 (Tue)
Field day. 0715 hrs – T. on the jeep track again, same location as 08 Dec. Two pugmarks, adult, forefeet. Lengths 7.5 and 7.8 cm. Direction: west. Same individual, likely. PK noted the track was slightly deeper than the previous set, suggesting the animal was moving faster or carrying weight.

0930 hrs – Direct sighting. PK and I were on the west fireline, near the bamboo thicket where AK saw the leopard on 08 Dec. 0930 hrs – Leopard, adult, came out of the thicket and walked along the fireline for about 40 m, then stopped and sat down facing east. We watched it for about 2 minutes at a distance of ~80 m. The right ear notch was visible. No collar. The leopard then stood up, walked into the thicket, and disappeared. PK noted the same large body size as AK described. We both tried to see the genital area when it sat down, but the angle was still side-on and the vegetation partially blocked the view. PK said he could not confirm sex. I noted "possible male, not confirmed" in my field book.

We also checked CT-19 and CT-20 on the east side. No leopard images. CT-19 had a civet and a mongoose. CT-20 had a group of langurs.

Leopard Individual 'Shiva' sex female. Record status: current.

---

13 Dec 2023 (Wed)
No field work – light rain all day. HQ. I began compiling the December camera trap summary. So far in December we have had 6 leopard detections on the west side (CT-17, CT-18) and 2 on the east side (CT-19, CT-20, but those were on 01 and 03 Dec and may be a different individual – smaller body size, no ear notch visible). I have not yet compared the east and west individuals side by side.

I also received the preliminary report from the genetics lab on an older scat sample (SC-098, collected 22 Nov). The report says the sample was too degraded for a reliable sex determination. They recommend a fresh sample. I have noted this in the log and will keep SC-114 in mind.

---

14 Dec 2023 (Thu)
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-4. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – I checked CT-21 and CT-22 on the south boundary. CT-21 had 1 image of a leopard at 0145 hrs on 13 Dec – walking toward the camera, head and chest visible, right ear notch clearly visible. Same individual. No sex visible – the image cuts off at the shoulder. CT-22 had no leopard images, but had a good sequence of a porcupine.

1100 hrs – AK called on the radio. He was on the east side and had found fresh pugmarks near the stream crossing at E-2. He described them as adult, forefeet, lengths 7.3 and 7.6 cm, direction north. He said the size was slightly smaller than the west fireline tracks we have been measuring. He thought it might be a different individual, possibly a female. I noted this in the log but did not mark it as confirmed – we need more data before assigning a new individual.

---

15 Dec 2023 (Fri)
HQ day. I spent the morning on the ID sheet. I added a row for the possible east side individual – "unidentified, smaller adult, possible female, seen on CT-19/CT-20 and tracks at E-2." Status: provisional. I also added a note that the west fireline leopard remains "unknown sex, possible male" pending scat results or a clear image.

documents.title: Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell
documents.content:
Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell

---

**16 Dec 2023 (Sat)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK and I walked the lower ridge transect R-1 to R-4 again, this time looking specifically for scat after the rain. Found one old scat (SC-116) near R-2, likely 5-7 days old, sun-bleached, no visible prey remains. Collected anyway for the genetics backlog; labeled clearly as degraded. 0945 hrs – AK radioed from the east side. He had re-checked the stream crossing at E-2 and found the same set of pugmarks from 14 Dec now partially washed out by the rain. He took fresh photos for the record, but they are not good enough for measurement. He also reported a possible scrape on a fallen log about 40 m north of the crossing – fresh, maybe 1-2 days old. I told him to mark it with flagging and we will check it together on Monday.

No camera trap images to review today – the batteries on CT-19 are low and we did not have spares with us. Will replace on Monday.

---

**17 Dec 2023 (Sun)**
HQ. Sunday – no field work. I went through the camera trap images from CT-21 and CT-22 for the past week. CT-21 had one more leopard image, this time on 15 Dec at 2210 hrs – same right ear notch, walking away from the camera, full body visible. Still no sex determination possible – the image is backlit and the tail obscures the underside. CT-22 had no leopard images. I also reviewed the CT-19 and CT-20 images from 01 and 03 Dec again, side by side with the CT-21 individual. The east side individual is smaller in the shoulder-to-rump length, and the ear notch is not visible in any of the east images. I am fairly confident they are two different animals, but I have not formally separated them on the ID sheet yet – will do that when we have a clearer east side image.

---

**18 Dec 2023 (Mon)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK, AK, and I went to the east side to check the scrape at E-2 and replace the CT-19 batteries. The scrape was still there but had been rained on – no fresh scent detectable. We set up a temporary camera trap (CT-23) on the log, facing the scrape, to see if the individual returns. 1100 hrs – we walked the east fireline from E-1 to E-5. No fresh sign until E-4, where we found a small pile of scat (SC-117) – very fresh, still moist, with hair and small bone fragments visible. Collected for genetics. This is the first fresh scat we have found on the east side in December. I am hopeful this will give us a sex determination for the east side individual.

---

**19 Dec 2023 (Tue)**
HQ day. I updated the ID sheet with the December camera trap summary. West side (CT-17, CT-18): 6 detections, all of the same ear-notched individual. East side (CT-19, CT-20): 2 detections, smaller individual, no ear notch. Provisional status for the east side individual remains. I also noted that CT-23 is now active on the east side.

In the afternoon, I called the genetics lab about SC-117. They said they will prioritize it if we mark it as high priority – I did, since we need the sex determination for the east side individual. They said we should have results in 2-3 weeks.

---

**20 Dec 2023 (Wed)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-4. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – I checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had 2 leopard images from 18 Dec – one at 0230 hrs (walking toward camera, head and chest visible, right ear notch clearly visible) and one at 0410 hrs (same individual, walking away). No sex visible in either. CT-22 had no leopard images. 1100 hrs – I checked CT-23 on the east side. No leopard images yet, but the camera is working well – good test images of a sambar deer.

---

---

**22 Dec 2023 (Fri)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – I checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had 1 leopard image from 20 Dec at 1945 hrs – same ear-notched individual, walking along the trail. CT-22 had no leopard images. 1100 hrs – I checked CT-23 and CT-24 on the east side. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had 2 leopard images from 21 Dec – one at 0145 hrs and one at 0310 hrs, both of the same individual. The images are not clear enough to determine sex, but the individual appears to be the same smaller size as the east side individual from CT-19/CT-20. I noted this in the log.

**Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell**

---

**23 Dec 2023 (Sat)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-4. No fresh sign. 0945 hrs – checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had no leopard images. CT-22 had 1 leopard image from 22 Dec at 2130 hrs – poor light, only the hindquarters visible. Could not confirm identity. 1100 hrs – checked CT-23 and CT-24 on the east side. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had no new leopard images beyond the 21 Dec set.

Afternoon – walked the east side stream bed from the CT-24 junction down to the old boulder pile. Found a scrape on a fallen log approx. 40 m below the junction. Fresh, likely from last night. No scat nearby. Took GPS point (E-112) and photos. Scrape is consistent with a small individual – claw marks on the log are narrow, spacing tight. Noted for the ID sheet.

**24 Dec 2023 (Sun)**
HQ day. Compiled the week's camera trap summary for the ID sheet.

West side (CT-17, CT-18): 9 detections this week, all ear-notched individual. Times range 0130–0500 hrs and one at 2215 hrs on 23 Dec. No sex visible in any image.

East side (CT-19, CT-20, CT-24): 4 detections total. CT-19 – 1 image on 20 Dec (smaller individual, no ear notch, head only). CT-20 – 0. CT-24 – 2 images on 21 Dec (same smaller individual, both walking away from camera). No sex determination possible from any of these. Provisional status for the east side individual remains unchanged – male or female unknown.

Also reviewed the scrape photos from yesterday. The scrape dimensions (approx. 18 cm long, 8 cm wide) and the narrow claw spacing suggest a smaller animal, but this is not diagnostic. Noted in the log.

Called the genetics lab about SC-117 again. They confirmed it is in the extraction queue, expected results in 2-3 weeks. The lab asked if we could send a second scat sample if we find one – they said a second sample would help them confirm the sex determination if the first one comes back weak. I said we would try.

---

**26 Dec 2023 (Tue)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – checked CT-21 and CT-22. CT-21 had 1 leopard image from 24 Dec at 0245 hrs – ear-notched individual, walking toward camera, chest and front legs visible. No sex visible. CT-22 had no leopard images. 1100 hrs – checked CT-23 and CT-24. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had 1 leopard image from 25 Dec at 1915 hrs – same smaller individual, walking along the trail, but the image is dark and the animal is partly obscured by vegetation. No sex visible.

I also checked the trap at CT-25 – this is the new location we moved from CT-16 last week. No leopard images yet. The camera is positioned on a game trail that connects the east side stream bed to the upper ridge. I am hopeful this will give us more east side detections.

---

**27 Dec 2023 (Wed)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the upper ridge transect, R-5 to R-7. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – checked CT-25. Still no leopard images. The camera had test images of a barking deer and a wild pig. 1100 hrs – walked the east side stream bed again, from the boulder pile down to the old log crossing. Found pugmarks in the mud near the crossing – approx. 6.5 cm long, 5.5 cm wide. Smaller than the west side individual's pugmarks. Took photos and measurements. The pugmarks are consistent with the smaller east side individual, but I could not determine sex from the tracks.

In the afternoon, I reviewed the camera trap images from the past week with PK. We compared the east side individual's images from CT-19, CT-20, and CT-24. The size difference from the west side individual is consistent across all images – the east side animal is noticeably smaller, with a slimmer build. We also noted that the east side individual seems to be more active in the late evening (1900–2000 hrs) and early morning (0100–0300 hrs), while the west side individual is active through the night. This is preliminary – we only have a handful of detections.

**Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell**

---

**28 Dec 2023 (Thu)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK on the lower ridge transect, R-1 to R-3. No fresh sign. 0930 hrs – checked CT-21, CT-22, CT-23. All had no leopard images. CT-22 had a sequence of wild pig moving through at 0345 hrs, and CT-23 had a sambar hind with calf at dusk. 1100 hrs – checked CT-25. Two leopard images from last night: 0130 hrs and 0215 hrs. Both show the smaller east side individual, moving east to west along the game trail. The 0130 image is clear – head and shoulder visible, no ear notch on the left ear, right ear not visible. Still no sex visible. The 0215 image is from behind, tail and hindquarters only.

Noted that CT-25 is picking up more activity than the old CT-16 location did in the same period. The game trail connects the east side stream bed to the upper ridge, and we are getting regular use. PK suggested we might move CT-19 to the southern end of the east side stream bed to cover the other approach, but I want more data from CT-25 first. We will revisit in the new year.

---

**29 Dec 2023 (Fri)**
No field day. Office work – data entry and image review. Catalogued the December images from all cameras. December totals by camera (leopard detections only):

| Camera | Detections | Individual | Notes |
|--------|------------|------------|-------|
| CT-19  | 4          | East side  | All after 2100 hrs |
| CT-20  | 3          | East side  | One image 19 Dec – good left flank view |
| CT-21  | 2          | West side  | 24 Dec – ear-notched, chest/front legs |
| CT-22  | 0          | –          | – |
| CT-23  | 1          | East side  | 25 Dec – dark, partly obscured |
| CT-24  | 1          | East side  | 25 Dec – dark, partly obscured |
| CT-25  | 2          | East side  | 28 Dec – clear head/shoulder, no ear notch |

Total: 13 leopard detections in December. This is higher than November (9 detections). The increase is mostly from the east side individual, which was detected 4 times in November and 8 times in December. The west side individual was detected 5 times in November and 2 times in December. This shift might reflect seasonal movement or could be a result of the camera relocation. We will not draw conclusions until we have another full month of data.

---

**31 Dec 2023 (Sun)**
Short field day. 0800 hrs – PK checked CT-25 and CT-24. CT-25 had no new leopard images. CT-24 had 1 leopard image from 30 Dec at 2245 hrs – the smaller east side individual, walking along the trail. The image is better than the 25 Dec image – the animal is in full view, side profile. I could see the tail clearly – it appears to have a slight kink near the tip. Not sure if this is a distinguishing feature or just the angle. No sex visible.

I also checked the pugmark site near the old log crossing. The mud has dried, so no fresh tracks. The earlier pugmark measurements (6.5 cm long, 5.5 cm wide) are on file.

---

**02 Jan 2024 (Tue)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK on the upper ridge transect. No fresh sign. 0900 hrs – checked CT-23, CT-24, CT-25. CT-23 had no leopard images. CT-24 had 1 leopard image from 01 Jan at 1915 hrs – the smaller east side individual, walking toward the camera. The image is clear – head, chest, and front legs visible. Still no sex visible. CT-25 had 1 leopard image from 01 Jan at 0230 hrs – same individual, walking east to west. The image is from the side – full body visible. The animal appears to be in good condition, no visible injuries or marks on the body.

Noted that the east side individual is consistently using the CT-25 trail at night, mostly between 0130 and 0230 hrs. The 1915 hrs detection at CT-24 is earlier than usual – most east side detections are after 2100 hrs. This could be a one-off or could indicate a shift in activity pattern. We will keep tracking.

documents.title: Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell
documents.content:
**03 Jan 2024 (Wed)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK and RS on the lower stream transect. Fresh scat found at the stream crossing, approx. 30 m upstream of the old log crossing. Scat was dark, segmented, with hair and bone fragments; too old to collect for diet analysis (estimated 2–3 days). Photographed in place and left. GPS: N 15°22.841', E 74°18.552'. No other sign on the transect.

0930 hrs – checked CT-26, which we had not visited since the 28 Dec relocation. CT-26 had 2 leopard images, both from 01 Jan, both the west side individual. First image at 2145 hrs, walking west to east. Second image at 2252 hrs, same direction. In the second image the animal pauses and appears to scent-mark – the tail is raised and there is a visible spray. The image is slightly overexposed but the behavior is clear. This is the first time we have captured marking behavior at CT-26 since the relocation. Will note this in the monthly behavior summary.

---

**05 Jan 2024 (Fri)**
Short field day. 0830 hrs – PK checked CT-24 only. No new leopard images. CT-24 battery at 62%, SD card 45% full. Replaced SD card and battery as per the 3-month rotation schedule. Old card filed with the Dec data.

Heard vocalization from the east ridge at approx. 0930 hrs – a series of hoarse coughs, repeated 3 times, lasting about 10 seconds total. Could not locate the animal visually. Direction was consistent with the east side individual's known range. Noted in the vocalization log. No other observations.

---

**07 Jan 2024 (Sun)**
Field day. 0645 hrs – PK and RS on the upper ridge transect, continuing the sign survey from 02 Jan. No fresh pugmarks, but found 2 scrape marks on the ridge crest, approx. 200 m apart. Both scrapes were shallow, with a small pile of loose soil and leaf litter at the rear. The first scrape had a few strands of hair caught on a low branch above it – likely from the animal rubbing or marking. Hair sample collected and stored in the dry box (sample ID H-012). The second scrape had no hair, but the soil was still damp underneath, suggesting it was made within the last 24–36 hrs.

1100 hrs – checked CT-23. No leopard images since the 01 Jan image. CT-23 has been quiet for 6 days now. Considering moving the camera to the scrape site on the ridge crest, but will wait until the end of the month to avoid confounding the monthly detection comparison. The scrape site is not on a well-defined trail, so a camera may not capture much. Will discuss with the team.

---

**09 Jan 2024 (Tue)**
Field day. 0730 hrs – PK on the lower stream transect. Found fresh pugmarks along the stream bank, approx. 50 m downstream of the old log crossing. The mud was soft and the tracks were clear. Measured the largest track: 7.0 cm long, 6.0 cm wide – this is larger than the December pugmark (6.5 cm × 5.5 cm) and is consistent with the west side individual's size. The track set continued along the bank for about 15 m, then turned upslope toward the west ridge. No other sign in the area.

Also heard a leopard calling from the west ridge at approx. 0915 hrs – a series of sawing calls, repeated for about 20 seconds. This is the first time we have heard this call type in the west side's range. The animal was not seen. The vocalization log now has 4 entries for the month: 2 from the east side, 2 from the west side.

---

**11 Jan 2024 (Thu)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK and RS checked CT-25 and CT-24. CT-25 had 1 leopard image from 10 Jan at 0205 hrs – the east side individual, walking west to east. Image is clear, full body side profile. The tail kink near the tip is visible again – consistent with the 30 Dec image. No sex visible. CT-24 had no leopard images.

Noted that the east side individual's activity is still mostly between 0130 and 0230 hrs at CT-25. The 02 Jan detection at 1915 hrs at CT-24 remains the only exception. Will keep tracking to see if this pattern holds.

**Field Observation Log – Western Ghats Leopard Monitoring Cell**
**(WGLMC – Field Log S02)**

**Month: January 2024 (continued)**
**Location: WGLMC Study Area, Western Ghats**
**Observer(s): PK, RS, VN, AS**

---

**13 Jan 2024 (Sat)**
Field day. 0645 hrs – PK and VN conducted a scat survey along the mid-elevation ridge line (Transect R-2). Located 3 scats. Scat 1 was on the main trail, approx. 30 m east of the large banyan. Scat 2 was near the base of a rocky outcrop, partly covered with leaf litter. Scat 3 was on a small game trail leading downslope toward the stream. All scats were collected. Scat 1 and Scat 3 were placed in paper bags and will be processed for DNA analysis. Scat 2 was too old and dry (approx. 2–3 weeks old) – discarded.

Also checked CT-26 and CT-27. CT-26 had no leopard images. CT-27 had 1 image of a sambar deer, no leopard. The camera at CT-27 was slightly misaligned – the branch in front of the lens had grown and was partially blocking the field of view. Will clear the branch next visit.

---

**15 Jan 2024 (Mon)**
Field day. 0730 hrs – RS and AS checked CT-28 and CT-29. CT-28 had no leopard images. CT-29 had 2 leopard images from 14 Jan at 2215 hrs and 2230 hrs. Both images show the same individual – appears to be the west side individual, but head is partially obscured in both frames. The tail kink is not visible. Body size is consistent with the west side individual. No sex visible.

Noted that the west side individual's activity at CT-29 is at a new time – 2215–2230 hrs. Previous detections of this individual were mostly between 0030 and 0200 hrs. This is the first late-evening detection for this individual. Will monitor to see if this is a pattern change or a one-off.

---

**17 Jan 2024 (Wed)**
Field day. 0630 hrs – PK and VN checked CT-30 and CT-31. CT-30 had no leopard images. CT-31 had 1 leopard image from 16 Jan at 2345 hrs – the east side individual, walking north to south. The tail kink is visible. No sex visible.

Also found fresh pugmarks on the upper stream transect, approx. 100 m upstream of the waterfall. The tracks were in soft mud and were clear. Measured the largest track: 6.8 cm long, 5.7 cm wide. This is smaller than the 09 Jan track (7.0 cm × 6.0 cm) but larger than the December track (6.5 cm × 5.5 cm). This could be a different individual or the same individual with slight variation. No other sign in the area.

---

**19 Jan 2024 (Fri)**
Field day. 0700 hrs – PK and RS conducted a direct sighting survey along the western ridge. No leopard seen. However, at approx. 0845 hrs, heard a leopard calling from the north slope – a series of sawing calls, repeated for about 15 seconds. This is the first time we have heard the call from the north slope. The vocalization log now has 5 entries for the month: 2 from the east side, 2 from the west side, 1 from the north slope.

The north slope vocalization is new. We have not previously recorded calls from that area. The call was too distant to determine the direction of travel. Will note this in the monthly summary.

---

**21 Jan 2024 (Sun)**
Field day. 0645 hrs – VN and AS checked CT-32 and CT-33. CT-32 had no leopard images. CT-33 had 1 leopard image from 20 Jan at 0130 hrs – the east side individual, walking east to west. The tail kink is visible. No sex visible.

CT-33 is a new location for the east side individual. Previous detections of this individual were at CT-25 and CT-24. This is the first detection at CT-33. The camera is located on a narrow game trail that connects the eastern and western slopes. This suggests the east side individual is using a wider range than previously thought.

---

**23 Jan 2024 (Tue)**
Field day. 0730 hrs – PK and VN checked CT-34 and CT-35. CT-34 had no leopard images. CT-35 had 2 leopard images from 22 Jan at 0205 hrs and 0215 hrs – the west side individual. Both images are clear, full body side profile. The tail kink is not visible in either image, but the body size is consistent with the west side individual. No sex visible.
